gap: Two of the three r9 faults are genuinely dead and I will not re-litigate them. THE GHOST SEARCH FIELD IS NOT REAL ON THIS BUILD. At 1.1x zoom on the panel's top-left corner there is exactly one bordered control: a rounded tan-outlined field carrying a magnifier and 'Search invoices'. Directly above it is the navy header bar and the window's rounded corner. Under the old rotateX(6) rotateY(-16) rotate(-5) that corner sheared into a second parallel rounded edge one field-height up, and I read it as a duplicated search box. It was the tilt, not a duplicate. Flattening removed it. THE CHECKBOX FAULT IS ALSO DEAD, and I measured rather than eyeballed it. Dark-pixel band centroids at native 2x, checkbox column vs customer-name column: header 948.5 vs 943.5, Northwind 1021.5 vs 1017.5, Harbour Point 1095.0 vs 1089.5, Studio Meridian 1166.5 vs 1162.5. That is a mean 4.6 native px, 2.3 CSS px. The residual rotate(-1.5) alone predicts 3.1 native px across the 118px gap between checkbox centre and label centre, so under 1 CSS px is real misalignment. r9 called it a third of a row height, roughly 14 CSS px. It is gone. The flattening is the right call and it worked: every cell now shares a baseline, 'Northwind Trading Co.' sits level with 'May 12' and '$4,820.50', and the panel reads at 100% the way Wave's dead-flat Transactions table does. The two mocks do now state one account: 4,820.50 / 12,500.75 / 2,140.25 / 863.40 in both, same four customers, same four dates, same $20,324.90. The Arabic mock is the strongest single artefact on either page and I want that on the record: a true RTL flip with the Latin customer names holding their place while the columns reverse, translated chrome, its own '+ فاتورة جديدة' primary control. Wave has nothing that demonstrates a capability a competitor could not fake. IT STILL LOSES, on one fault that is fatal in category rather than merely ugly. THE HERO'S TOTALS ROW MAKES AN ACCOUNTING CLAIM ITS OWN ROWS DISPROVE. The label reads 'Total outstanding' and the figure is $20,324.90, which is the sum of ALL FOUR rows. But row 1 Northwind $4,820.50 is stamped Paid, row 3 Cedar Clinic $2,140.25 is stamped Paid, and row 4 Studio Meridian $863.40 is stamped Draft. Only Harbour Point's $12,500.75 is Overdue. So the flagship image of an accounting product tells the reader a business is owed $20,324.90 while, four lines above, it says $6,960.75 of that is already collected and $863.40 was never issued. Outstanding means unpaid in every product this one is sold against. No ERP has ever totalled paid invoices into outstanding, and the buyer for this page is the one person who spots it in four seconds. r9 forced the two mocks to agree on the NUMBER and they now do; nobody forced them to agree on what the number MEANS, and the page's own second mock proves the right answer was already in the codebase, because AppMockup labels the identical $20,324.90 'الإجمالي' / 'Total', with no outstanding claim attached. The hero invented the error on its own. Wave never does this: its equivalent line is 'All Accounts $25,980.23', an account balance, a statement of fact the rows cannot contradict. SECOND, the 'Currency billing / Any' chip still names a control it does not touch, unchanged from r9 point four. Its tail lands on the sidebar-to-table divider beside 'Reports & Analytics', while the USD/EUR/AED segmented toggle it is describing sits in the opposite corner, about 320 native px up and 800 px across. The source even carries a comment calling that toggle 'the currency control the any-currency chip points at', so the intent is written down and the render does not honour it. The sibling chip proves the idiom works when it is aimed: 'Languages supported / 5' tails down into the navy header and lands on the real globe+EN control. THIRD, the two mocks still render the same status two different ways. In the hero, 'Paid' is bare green text with no pill while 'Overdue' and 'Draft' get pills; in the Arabic mock all three of مدفوعة, متأخرة and مسودة sit on pills. Under a headline reading 'Your data stays the same, only the interface changes', a status badge that is a chip in one shot and loose text in the other says the interface changed something other than the language. FOURTH, mobile is closer than r9 allowed but still behind. Wave's phone fold carries no product panel either, only two complete legible tag chips, 'Main Street Reno Project' and 'Summer Campaign'; ours carries one chip plus a sliver of navy chrome reading 'Invoices EN', with no row, no amount and no status above the fold. Two finished elements beat one finished element and one truncated corner. THE FIX, in priority order: make the hero's totals row true. Either relabel it 'Total' to match the line the second mock already gets right, or keep 'Total outstanding' and print $12,500.75, the one row actually outstanding, with the paid and draft rows excluded from the sum. Second, re-anchor the 'Currency billing / Any' chip so its tail lands on the USD/EUR/AED toggle, or move the toggle down to the chip. Third, pick one status treatment, pill or bare text, and use it in both mocks. Fourth, lift the panel enough that the phone fold shows one complete row with its amount and its status pill.
